the-principles-of-aesthetics: Philosopher De Witt Parker asks a timeless question in this clear-minded book: what makes something beautiful? He examines painting, music, poetry, and architecture to explain how art works on the human mind and feelings. Written as a college text in 1920, it remains a friendly entry point into the philosophy of art for readers with no background in the subject.
study-and-stimulants-or-the-use-of-intox: A. Arthur Reade examines how alcohol and drugs affect the working mind — with arguments aimed at students and brain-workers. Drawing on science and example, he makes the temperance case in intellectual terms. A period piece now, but an interesting one in the history of attitudes toward drink.
